title: Paloma and the Crown
premise: Lena Vasquez has survived five years as a royal food-taster in Vhalen, a city where magic is outlawed and her small charms are a death sentence if discovered. When the old gods suddenly begin answering prayers again, Lena discovers her taster's immunity is itself a half-forgotten blessing — and that the king on the throne died years ago, his body worn like a glove by the usurper's crown-spirit. Hunted by the crown's witch-hunters and guided by a disgraced priestess and a god who remembers her grandmother, Lena must gather the scattered relics of the true coronation rite and unbind the dead king before the usurper's armies reach the free cities. In the end she learns inheritance cannot be refused, only chosen: she takes up the unbinding herself, crowns no one, and gives the old gods back to the people who prayed to them.
about_author: Hazel Pemberton is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk charms and household blessings before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about ordinary people who inherit impossible things, and lives near the sea with an unreasonable number of houseplants.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She tastes the king's breakfast, detects poison, and quietly pockets a silver charm from a frightened kitchen boy. Establishes her double life: loyal servant by day, illegal charm-seller by night. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Small Gods, Small Prices
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In the Nightmarket she sells protective knots and luck-threads to dockworkers, breaking the Edict of Ash one charm at a time. A customer's prayer is answered for the first time in years — audibly. Emotional beat: wonder edged with terror.

chapters.title: The Edict of Ash
chapters.summary: Witch-hunter Captain Sorrel's POV. He interrogates a charm-seller and finds a ledger bearing Lena's mark. Introduces the state's fear of returning divinity. Emotional beat: cold duty beginning to crack into doubt.

chapters.title: What the Soup Remembered
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The broth she tastes tastes back — it shows her a memory of her grandmother praying at a drowned shrine. Her immunity, she realizes, was never chemistry. Emotional beat: vertigo of self-discovery.

chapters.title: The King Who Did Not Blink
chapters.summary: Court steward Maren's POV. During an audience, Maren notices the king never blinks, never sweats, never ages. She begins keeping a private record. Emotional beat: creeping dread dressed as loyalty.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered Wrong
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The dockworker from chapter two dies smiling, his wish granted too literally. Lena understands the returning gods are raw, unfiltered, dangerous. Emotional beat: guilt and responsibility.

chapters.title: The Priestess in the Cistern
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Fleeing Sorrel's raid on the Nightmarket, she shelters with Odile, a disgraced priestess hiding beneath the city, who recognizes the blessing in Lena's blood. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Crown-Spirit
chapters.summary: The usurper's POV (unnamed). We enter the thing wearing the king: it reviews troop movements toward the free cities and senses, distantly, that a god has woken. Emotional beat: patient hunger.

chapters.title: Immunity Is a Kind of Love
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She explains the old rite: royal tasters were blessed vessels, immune so they could carry messages between gods and kings. Lena's line was meant for this. Emotional beat: grief for a stolen inheritance.

chapters.title: Sorrel Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Sorrel confronts her at the palace with the ledger; she talks her way free but must now spy for him or be burned. Emotional beat: trapped, resourceful, furious.

chapters.title: The First Relic: Salt
chapters.summary: Lena and Odile retrieve consecrated salt from a flooded chapel while the tide rises. First trial of the unbinding rite. Emotional beat: fear overcome together.

chapters.title: Letters to a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. She finds the king's private correspondence stops five years ago mid-sentence, and matches the date to the night of the 'miraculous recovery.' Emotional beat: horror of confirmation.

chapters.title: The God Who Remembers Grandmothers
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. At the drowned shrine, a small god speaks to her in her grandmother's voice, offering help at the price of being remembered. Emotional beat: tenderness entangled with manipulation.

chapters.title: Free Cities, Burning Beacons
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs via intercepted dispatches read by Maren. The usurper's armies march; the free cities send desperate envoys the crown ignores. Emotional beat: the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Charm-Seller's Confession
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Under Sorrel's questioning she confesses only the charms, protecting Odile, and watches him hesitate over the sentence. Emotional beat: moral friction between hunter and hunted.

chapters.title: The Second Relic: Bread
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She steals coronation bread from the palace's own ovens using her taster's access, nearly caught by Maren — who lets her pass without a word. Emotional beat: unexpected complicity.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Usurper's POV. It summons Sorrel, senses his doubt, and offers him promotion in exchange for the taster's head. Emotional beat: seduction of power.

chapters.title: Odile's Fall
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Flashback to the purge that destroyed her order and why she stopped praying. She admits she fears the gods more than loves them. Emotional beat: shame confronted.

chapters.title: The Third Relic: Blood
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The rite requires royal blood; the only royals left are the dead king's body and Lena's own tainted-by-service veins. She chooses to offer hers. Emotional beat: costly consent.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Gate
chapters.summary: Sorrel's POV. Torn between oath and conscience, he leads witch-hunters to the cistern — then misdirects them at the last moment. Emotional beat: defection begun, not finished.

chapters.title: Midnight Coronation
chapters.summary: Lena, Odile, and Maren perform the unbinding rite in the throne room. It fails: the crown-spirit has been feeding on the king's memories for years and knows every counterword. Emotional beat: devastating setback.

chapters.title: The King Beneath
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Deep under the failure, she hears the real king — a flicker of the man — begging not to be saved but to be remembered. Emotional beat: compassion reframes the mission.

chapters.title: Prisoners of the Palace
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Arrested on suspicion, Maren endures interrogation, protecting the others through bureaucratic stonewalling. Emotional beat: quiet courage.

chapters.title: The Army at the River
chapters.summary: Usurper's POV. The host reaches the last river before the free cities; the crown-spirit prepares a mass rite to devour the cities' prayers as fuel. Emotional beat: scale of the threat revealed.

chapters.title: Nightmarket Rising
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She returns to the ruins of the Nightmarket and finds the charm-sellers organizing — thousands of small illegal blessings, ready to be used. Emotional beat: hope through community.

chapters.title: Sorrel's Choice
chapters.summary: Sorrel's POV. Ordered to burn the Nightmarket survivors, he instead burns his own warrant and joins Lena, bringing the witch-hunters' secret files. Emotional beat: redemption paid for.

chapters.title: The Fourth Relic: Name
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The final relic is the king's true name, erased from all records by the usurper. Only Maren's private records hold fragments. Emotional beat: archives as resistance.

chapters.title: March of the Small Gods
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The charm-bearers march on the capital carrying waking minor gods; prayers spark along the road like fire in dry grass. Emotional beat: exultant momentum.

chapters.title: What the Crown Knows
chapters.summary: Usurper's POV. The crown-spirit confronts its own origin: it was once a god of order, starved into hunger by the Edict itself. Emotional beat: villainy given tragic roots.

chapters.title: Siege of the Palace Gates
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The city rises; palace guards defect; Sorrel holds the gate against loyalist hunters. Emotional beat: chaos with purpose.

chapters.title: Maren's Ledger
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Escaping custody, she delivers the name-fragments, completing the true name at terrible personal cost — she is wounded shielding the pages. Emotional beat: sacrifice of the faithful clerk.

chapters.title: The Unbinding, Second Attempt
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. With salt, bread, blood, and name, she begins the rite as the crown-spirit floods the throne room with armies of memory. Emotional beat: terror and resolve.

chapters.title: Inside the Crown
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, visionary. Pulled into the king's worn body, she walks his five stolen years and finds him kneeling in his own mind, waiting for someone to say his name. Emotional beat: intimate heartbreak.

chapters.title: The Name Spoken
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She speaks King Aldric's name; he chooses, at last, to die rather than be restored as a vessel, taking much of the crown-spirit with him. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into release.

chapters.title: The Hungry God Unmasked
chapters.summary: Climax continues, multiple POVs. The remainder of the crown-spirit breaks loose and turns on the city; the small gods and charm-bearers hold it at the gates in a battle fought with prayers and charms. Emotional beat: collective courage against overwhelming power.

chapters.title: A Crown Refused
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Victorious factions demand she take the throne as the blessed taster; she refuses, arguing no single vessel should hold the gods again. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh — inheritance chosen, not seized.

chapters.title: The Rite of Many Hands
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. They invent a new coronation: authority distributed among councils, guilds, and the returned gods' shrines. Odile re-prays for the first time in twenty years. Emotional beat: healing institutions and faith.

chapters.title: After the Ash
chapters.summary: Sorrel's POV. The Edict is repealed; Sorrel helps rebuild the Nightmarket instead of burning it, and takes honest work guarding it. Emotional beat: restitution.

chapters.title: Charms for Free
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She gives away her last sold charm, opens a school for tasters-and-listeners, and visits Aldric's grave with bread and salt. Emotional beat: peace earned, memory kept.

chapters.title: Paloma
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Lena's POV. At the drowned shrine, the small god gives her a new name — Paloma, the dove that carried messages between gods and kings — and she accepts it not as a title but as a promise. The free cities stand; the gods listen; the story closes on a prayer answered gently. Emotional beat: belonging at last.
